 Oral Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimants assailing the judgment and award dated 08.02.2019, in MVC No.130/2016, on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.13, Vijayapur (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal'), dismissing the claim petition.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.13, Vijayapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of brevity, the parties in the appeal shall be referred to in terms of their status and ranking before the Tribunal.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:850 HC-KAR 3.

It is the case of the claimants that, on 06.10.2015, the husband of claimant No.1 - Sharanappa Khadakhade was travelling as a pillion rider in motorcycle bearing No.MH-13/BX-8659, being ridden by one Mallikarjun Biradar and on account of rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle in question, the deceased fell down from the motorcycle and thereafter, succumbed to injuries on Smt. Vimal And Ors vs Anil And Anr on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78120892/
2 07.10.2015.

sentences.text: Hence, the claimants have filed MVC No.130/2016 seeking compensation.
4. On service of notice, responded No.1 - owner of the vehicle in question though served remained absent and accordingly, he placed expert.
The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company contested the matter by filing objections.
In order to prove their case, the claimants have examined three witnesses as PW.1 to PW.3 and got marked ten documents as Exs.P1 to P10.

On the other hand,
respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked two documents as Exs.R1 and R2.

The Tribunal after considering the material on record, by its NC: 2026:KHC-K:850 HC-KAR judgment dated 08.02.2019, dismissed the claim petition and being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have preferred this appeal.

5. Heard Sri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants and Sri Sanjay M. Joshi, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.
6.

Sri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants invited the attention of the Court to paragraph No.20 of the impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal and contended that, the Tribunal has not properly appreciated the material on record, as the deceased died on account of the motor vehicle accident.

It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the claimants that, the Tribunal has failed to consider the documents produced by the claimants, as to MLC extract issued by the Ashwini Hospital at Solapur as per Ex.P5.
Therefore, he sought for interference of this Court.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:850 HC-KAR 7.

Per contra, Sri Sanjay M. Joshi, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company sought to justify the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in dismissing the claim petition.

8. Having taken note of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on careful consideration of the records, particularly, with regard to Ex.P1 - FIR, wherein, it is stated that, the motorcycle in which the deceased was travelling was ridden in rash and negligent manner and as such, the deceased fell down from the motorcycle.
It is also to be noted that, the motorcycle got skid on the road as per the complaint vide Ex.P1.
It is also to be noted from Exs.P7 - M.V. Report that, there was no scratch to the vehicle in question.

If that being the case, there was no impediment for the claimants to prove the alleged accident by examining respondent No.1 - owner of the vehicle in question and that effort has not been made by the claimants.
It is also to be noted that,
respondent
No.1 NC: 2026:KHC-K:850 HC-KAR though served with notice, however, remained absent and placed exparte.

9. In that view of the matter, taking into consideration the entire material on record and appreciation of the material by the Tribunal, particularly, with regard to the reasons assigned at paragraph No.20 of the impugned judgment, I am of the view that, there is no perversity in the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, no interference is called for in this appeal.
